title: Lattice-intersection embedding of a sharp fs monoid
statement: Let $P$ be a finitely generated integral saturated commutative monoid, written additively, with group completion $G=P^{\rm gp}$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Assume $P$ is sharp: if $a,b\in P$ and $a+b=0$, then $a=b=0$. Then there exist an integer $r\geq0$ and an injective group homomorphism $\lambda:G\to\mathbf Z^r$ such that $\lambda(P)=\lambda(G)\cap\mathbf N^r$, where $\mathbf N^r$ is the set of integer vectors with every coordinate nonnegative. In particular $\lambda|_P$ identifies $P$ with this intersection as an additive monoid. The cases $P=\{0\}$ and $r=0$ are allowed.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.17 (saturation) and 3.1.29 (rational polyhedral description), printed pp. 101 and 103, motivate this explicit lattice-intersection formulation. This formulation and its proof plan are by Q48, not a theorem quoted verbatim from those passages; see report.md. Kato 1994, Toric singularities, is WANTED for the underlying toric local algebra.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-sharp-cone-lattice-intersection] to the given $P$. With $G=P^{\rm gp}$ and $V=G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, it gives that $G$ is free abelian of finite rank, that the cone $C$ generated by $P$ is pointed, rational polyhedral and spanning, and that $P=C\cap G$ inside $V$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.17 and Remark 3.1.29, printed pp. 101 and 103.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-rational-cone-dual-integral-forms] to the lattice $G$ and cone $C$. Obtain $r$ and integral homomorphisms $\varphi_i:G\to\mathbf Z$ whose rational extensions span the dual of $V$ and satisfy $C=\{v: \varphi_i(v)\ge0\ \text{for all }i\}$.

source.place: Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103, with the integral dual-cone refinement recorded in the cited node.

proof.text: Define $\lambda:G\to\mathbf Z^r$ by $\lambda(g)=(\varphi_1(g),\ldots,\varphi_r(g))$. It is a group homomorphism. If $\lambda(g)=0$, then $g\otimes1$ is annihilated by every member of a spanning family of $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Q}(V,\mathbf Q)$, so $g\otimes1=0$; the torsion-freeness of the free abelian group $G$ from Step 1 gives $g=0$, hence $\lambda$ is injective. For $g\in G$, the coordinates of $\lambda(g)$ are all nonnegative exactly when $g\in C$, and Step 1 identifies this with $g\in P$. Therefore $\lambda(P)=\lambda(G)\cap\mathbf N^r$. Restriction to $P$ is consequently an additive-monoid identification. If $G=0$, the dual space is zero and the empty family gives $r=0$; this also covers $P=\{0\}$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q15-989c16a49 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The mathematics is correct and was read in full. Item: a fine saturated sharp monoid P admits an injective lambda:G->Z^r with lambda(P)=lambda(G)∩N^r. Step 1 (P=C∩G with C pointed and spanning, G free) and step 2 (Minkowski–Weyl with integral dual forms spanning the dual) are true; I checked the torsion-freeness, pointedness and saturation arguments. Step 3 is genuinely elementary (injectivity from the spanning forms plus torsion-freeness; orthant equality). Small cases checked: P=0, N, N^2, the cone on (1,0),(1,1), the A1 monoid; the non-sharp Z and the non-saturated <2,3> fail, as they should. The citer lem-trf-log-regular-saturation-normality needs exactly this statement. Sources: ILO VIII 3.1.17 (printed p.101) and Rem 3.1.29 (p.103) were read and only motivate the statement; proof_origin=agent and Kato is WANTED, which is correct. No SGA, no off-unit uses, no tool_uses. The new nodes are strictly smaller than the item and are not duplicates of the Gordan, finite-saturation or fs-face-sharpening nodes (face-sharpening with F=0 covers only clause (a)). Mathlib has no Minkowski–Weyl theorem (DualFinite.lean:21 mentions it only in its documentation).
